messages:
maria_chen: Heads-up: scheduling a rolling OS/security patch + graceful node reboots for the staging-edge cohort (az3) this Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC. We'll cordon/drain small groups to avoid large GPU capacity cliffs. Details below.

ops-oncall: What's the cohort size and expected concurrency impact? Any customer-facing windows? :eyes:

alex_k: Cohort = 10 nodes (~40 GPUs) out of a 480-GPU pool. Plan is 10-node batches every 30m with a 15m drain + reboot + 10m sanity. Peak concurrent capacity loss ~8-10%. Should be fine for staging but still want to avoid hitting autoscale thresholds.

sanjay: Cost/ops note: if autoscaler spins up replacements or we backfill on demand, estimate ~2.3k credits for the window (spot+ephemeral). Also watch for NIC firmware re-flaps we've seen after this OS version.

maria_chen: TL;DR runbook: cordon -> drain with eviction timeout 900s -> restart -> kubelet health checks -> uncordon. Use canary 1 batch on low-traffic hosts first.

alex_k: Commands we will use:
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=15m
# reboot via ansible: ansible -i inventory az3 -m reboot -l <node>
```
Keep probes green, do not force-evict pods older than 5m if they’re in-progress jobs.

ops-oncall: What about GPU KV cache / prefix-cache warming for staging services? We should pre-seed common model prefixes on the target nodes after reboot.

maria_chen: Good call — plan to run a lightweight prefix warmup job after the first successful node of batch-1. Schedule: warmup job runs 5m after node becomes Ready.

rachel_p: Customer comms: post to status page with the exact UTC window and that this is staging-only, no expected production impact. Also email a short note to early-access tenants who use az3. I can draft the message.

deploy-bot: Maintenance event created: "staging-edge az3 rolling OS patch" Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC. Reminder scheduled 1h before.

alex_k: Rollback plan: if >15% capacity lost or latency SLO breaches, pause and failover routing to eu/primary pools. We have a routing policy ready to shift traffic for canary keys.

sanjay: Ops checklist item: monitor NIC errors, BMC heartbeats, and kernel OOPS for 30m after each batch. If BMC flaps, escalate to hw-svc immediately.

maria_chen: Volunteers for midnight on-call to run the first two batches? Need 2 people for the first 90m.

ops-oncall: I can cover batch-1 and batch-2. Will post pager rotation and update runbook with exact node list.

rachel_p: Draft ready, will post to #customer-status and cc AE team once event confirmed.

maria_chen: Perfect — I'm going to lock the start time and publish the runbook in the maintenance doc. Ping here if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
